title: Bob the Canadian: on the road, part 2

lines.text: So the intersection behind me here is called a four-way stop or an all-way stop.
What that means is that whoever stops first at the intersection gets to go next.
So everyone needs to take turns going through this intersection.
Red lights mean stop and green lights mean go.
When that light comes on, it means there's a train coming.
I think I'm just in time to see this. Let's watch the train go by.
So that's why when that light's going, you should not cross the railroad track.
On the sides of the road you will see speed limit signs,
which tell you how fast you can drive your vehicle.
This is a speed limit sign from a city or town,
and it says you can do 50 kilometers an hour maximum.
It says you can do 80 kilometers an hour max,
and if you go any faster, you might get a ticket.
A guardrail stops vehicles from going off the road if they lose control.
This is a place for pedestrians to walk.
Pedestrians are people who are walking along the sidewalk.
Sometimes you'll even find a bike lane.
This is a six lane highway. It has three lanes going in either direction.
